slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Direct determination of inorganic phosphate: in acid medium it forms a yellow phosphomolybdate complex with ammonium molybdate (measured in the UV).
The colour intensity is proportional to the inorganic phosphorus concentration.
About 85% of body phosphorus is in bone and teeth.

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Phosphorus-UV” kit (IFU BSIS15-I, 08/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or plasma free of haemolysis, removed from the clot quickly (so phosphate does not leak from red cells); stable 7 days at 2–8 °C.
24-hour urine: collect into a bottle with 10 mL of 10% v/v hydrochloric acid; adjust to pH 2; dilute 1/10 and multiply the result by 10; 10 days at 2–8 °C.
Reagent: ammonium molybdate 0.40 mM, sulphuric acid 210 mM, detergents. Standard: phosphorus 5 mg/dL.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 340 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The reagent and standard are ready to use.
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light; particles or turbidity are signs of deterioration.
Detergents contain chelating agents and phosphates — rinse glassware with diluted nitric acid and water.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “Phosphorus-UV” IFU (BSIS15-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 340 nm; temperature 37 °C, 30 °C or 25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — reagent 1.0 mL; standard — reagent 1.0 mL + standard 10 µL; sample — reagent 1.0 mL + sample 10 µL.
4. Mix and incubate for 5 minutes.
5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: phosphorus programme
rows: Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (mg/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 5 (standard concentration).
24-hour urine: result × urine volume (dL/24 h) = mg/24 h. Conversion: mg/dL × 0.323 = mmol/L.
Linear up to 35 mg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference: adults 2.5–5.0 mg/dL (0.80–1.61 mmol/L), children 4.0–7.0 mg/dL (1.29–2.26 mmol/L); urine (adults) 0.4–1.3 g/24 h.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Haemolysed specimens are unacceptable: red-cell organic phosphate esters hydrolyse on storage and raise inorganic phosphate.
Late separation of serum from the clot falsely raises phosphorus.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Reagent: H290 — may be corrosive to metals; H314 — causes severe skin burns and eye damage.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
